paper.title: Language Identification in the Limit with Computational Trace
paper.summary: Identifies Turing-recognizable languages from accepting traces and determines the edit-error regimes permitting identification for finite automata, pushdown automata, and Turing machines.

formalization_scope.summary: All four numbered main theorems in Sections 3 and 4 have kernel-checked proofs. Both clauses of the pushdown and Turing robust identification results are included.
specializations: The robust theorems use the binary models specified in Section 4 and Appendix B.3. The pushdown model accepts by empty input and empty stack and permits silent steps.
The pushdown and Turing upper bounds use finite hypothesis descriptions with a bounded simulator and dovetailing, satisfying Definition 1. The DFA output has an explicit product automaton.
The perfect-trace learner accepts any injectively coded input alphabet. The error cutoff in every robust theorem measures the input word length.

claims.title: Turing identification from perfect traces
claims.statement_summary: A deterministic Turing recognizer is identifiable from a positive enumeration with its full accepting computations.

formalization.notes: The learner decodes each observed transition, including the written symbol and head direction. Its table stabilizes to the accepting fragment.

claims.title: Finite automata tolerate a constant edit rate
claims.statement_summary: For each known rate below one and known input-length cutoff, there is a learner identifying every binary DFA under the allowed trace corruptions.

formalization.notes: The proof uses two simple paths through a visited state, a finite enumeration of transition tables, and a product of the surviving DFAs.

claims.title: Diminishing versus constant error for pushdown machines
claims.statement_summary: Diminishing error admits identification of deterministic pushdown targets. Every positive constant rate admits a hard family.

formalization.notes: The upper bound uses a protected derivation and a finite candidate description. The lower bound erases the final pops of concrete deterministic block counters.

components.summary: A known diminishing-rate modulus admits identification.
Each positive constant rate admits a common-observation obstruction.

claims.title: Bounded versus diminishing error for Turing machines
claims.statement_summary: A fixed number of edits on each sufficiently long word permits identification. A single diminishing-error modulus suffices for a family on which every learner fails.

source_assessment.notes: Appendix B.3 applies an input-length cutoff to computation length in the proof of Lemma B.2. The Lean upper bound handles short inputs separately. Both conclusions of Theorem 4.5 are proved.

formalization.notes: The positive proof memorizes short words and simulates long positive examples for a bounded time. The negative proof uses a pre-halting quadratic padding routine with identical surviving configurations.

components.summary: A known per-example edit budget and input cutoff admit identification.
A known common diminishing-rate modulus admits an impossibility example.
